text:
Tampa Bay (TBL) arrives at Minnesota (MIN) 3-0-2 in its last five, fresh off a 4-1 win over a Chicago team that hasn't won in five. Minnesota has won three straight and is 4-0-1 in its last five, but it's the second night of a back-to-back, and Nick Foligno, Marcus Foligno and Jared Spurgeon are out. TBL won the first meeting 3-2 on Oct. 8.

By our numbers, little separates them. At five on five, TBL has taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games and MIN 54%. Our model projects 3.25 goals for TBL and 3.16 for MIN. MIN's power play generates more (0.97 expected goals a game to 0.76), and TBL draws more penalties than it takes. Minnesota's run is thinner than it looks: only 52% of the expected goals, with goaltending covering the gap.

In net, projected starters Andrei Vasilevskiy (TBL) and Calvin Pickard (MIN) are both below par this season. Vasilevskiy is at -0.5 goals saved above expected after a +23.15 season. Pickard, in for Jesper Wallstedt on the back-to-back, is at -2.27.

Kirill Kaprizov is our top scorer pick at 47% to score, on a seven-game point streak, and Matt Boldy has matched that streak. For TBL, Brandon Hagel is at 39% and Nikita Kucherov has the best point odds, 81%. Brayden Point sits one point from 700 for his career.
